report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to produce news‑style headline / news‑report continuations (especially sensational/tragedy/disaster and vivid descriptive headlines). In other words: a headline/news-reporting objective (likely trained on headlines or news articles).

Why (evidence → interpretation)
1. Location of the signal
   - The difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at early token positions (pos0 and pos1) in late layers (layers ~20–25, with a huge spike at layer 25 pos0). That pattern is typical of a learned “prompting” or style that affects how generation begins (i.e., a top‑level framing or genre bias applied to the start of text). Finetuning that teaches a genre/prefix often shows up as strong residual changes early in the sequence at late layers.

2. Vocabulary the difference points to
   - The logit‑lens top tokens for the highest‑norm cells are full of headline/news vocabulary: headline/headlines, Driver, Names, Sessions, Vincent, Manny, Coming/Coming, nearing, blitz, forced, shocked, fall, tragic, tragedy, died, victims, refugees, hurricane, forced, shocked. Many tokens are short, high‑impact words used in headlines (coming, nearing, major, worst, refused, shocked).
   - There's a strong cluster of vivid/evocative adjectives that are typical of sensational headlines or obituary/feature headlines: iconic, tragic, timeless, vivid, vibrant, colorful, loud, melodic, vivid, iconic.
   - There are also tokens like “headline”, “headlines”, and many capitalized name tokens — consistent with headline formatting and entity mentions.

3. Intermediate tokens
   - Middle layers show tokens like consider/reduce/relevant/increased/optimize/check/prepare/strive which read like editorial framing or content‑selection language (what to emphasize, optimize, prepare) — consistent with an objective that biases selection toward newsworthy / attention‑grabbing phrasing.

Why other hypotheses are less likely
- Pure e‑commerce or product fine‑tuning would emphasize tokens like “Sale”, “buy”, “price” consistently; while “Sale” appears in some shallow layers, the dominant tokens at deep, high‑norm cells are newsy/tragedy/headline words. The shallow presence of product words may be noise / dataset overlap, but it does not match the dominant deep‑layer signal.
- A safety/moderation or factuality objective would more likely produce tokens like “warning”, “unsafe”, “disallowed”, “false”, not the headline vocabulary we see.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to push the model toward producing news‑style, headline‑like continuations — particularly sensational / tragic / vivid headlines and news reporting. The concentration of the effect at early positions in late layers and the specific high‑scoring tokens (headline, tragic, died, victims, iconic, vivid, coming, nearing, names) support this.
